verdict.rationale: Insomnia's own mock servers (cloud, self-hosted Mockbin, dynamic, and AI-generated from a prompt, OpenAPI spec or live URL) give users a stand-in endpoint to test against instead of a live production API. Environments let users group variables such as base URLs, so requests can be pointed at non-production targets. However, nothing documents a sandbox mode that guarantees isolation from production data, or any production-protection guardrails for AI or agent-driven testing. Missing for 10: explicit sandbox/production isolation guarantees, documented guardrails preventing requests from reaching production, agent-specific sandbox workflows, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: The Insomnia Cloud mock servers allow you to create a mock endpoint in a few steps.
Users can deploy self-hosted mock servers using Insomnia Mockbin. This allows you to have more control over usage for your mocks.
Auto-generate a mock server from a natural language prompt and one of the following input types: URL, OpenAPI, or JSON.
Use environments to define groups of variables that Insomnia applies across your requests. For example, you could create variables for base URLs, tokens, or credentials.
